newsitem.title: UK: UK Lib Dems set to vote against budget tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: UK Lib Dems set to vote against budget tax cuts.

text.p: Britain's minority Liberal Democrats on Thursday pledged to vote against pre-election tax cuts they expect to be introduced in next Tuesday's annual budget.

Economics spokesman Malcolm Bruce told a news conference the party would rather spend the two billion pounds which the government would lose by reducing the standard rate of income tax by 1p in the pound on investment in education.
"We believe that monies from the Contingency Reserve could be found to fund this investment," Bruce told a news conference.

"But if the Chancellor (of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke) decides to cut taxes instead, then, given the high levels of public borrowing, we are prepared to vote to reverse a 1p reduction in the basic rate of tax."
The opposition Labour Party abstained on a Liberal motion in parliament disapproving of tax cuts made in last year's November budget.

Liberal leader Paddy Ashdown predicted it would take a similar stance this year, and then, in an act of "sheer, rank hypocrisy", criticise the government for the effect underfunding would have on services provided by local authorities.
"If taxes are cut substantially in this budget, it doesn't matter who the government are after the election -- those cuts will be reversed," he predicted.
Producing their alternative budget proposals, the Liberals called for an Office for Economic and Fiscal Assessment to be set up to examine government economic plans.
Ashdown said this would discourage governments from producing unrealistically rosy economic forecasts ahead of general elections to justify voter-pleasing tax cuts. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
